newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - French debt vols drop after poll result.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - French debt vols drop after poll result.

text.p: Implied volatility of French debt options on MATIF took a tumble on Monday, as investors scurried to take profits after the left-wing gained a surprise victory in the French election, traders said.
Implied volatility of June PIBOR options traded at a volatility of 42 percent, compared with a close of 56.1 percent on Friday, when pre-election fever pushed vols to highs of above 60 percent.
July notionnel options volatility fell to 5.7 percent, compared with a high of 6.8 percent on Friday, and a closing level of 6.5 percent.

"Talk of a delay to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) or the possibility of a weak euro are still paramount, but volatility got so high that the pressure had to be released," said a salesman at a European bank. "At the kind of levels we saw on Friday, people were tempted to take profits."
June notionnel futures were up 0.02 at 128.52 by 1430 GMT, while September was up 0.04 at 126.96. June PIBOR was up 0.03 at 96.39.
Socialist Lionel Jospin agreed to form a new government on Monday, after the combined left won 318 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, according to official final results.
Traders and brokers said there are concerns that the new French government will be unwilling to pursue the kind of austerity measures necessary to ensure France is in the first round of EMU.
Although volatility had fallen, traders said it would quickly find a floor while the EMU uncertainty remains a top priority.
"July (notionnel) would be a buy around 5.5 percent," said the European bank salesman.
September notionnel options vol was off 0.20 percent at 5.4 percent.
September PIBOR volatility fell to 28 percent, from 31.3 percent on Friday. July PIBOR was at 30 percent, off from 37.3 percent. The European bank salesman said July was a buy below 30 percent.
"There's been a lot of selling of July calls at 96.60/70 strikes to buy June," said Jonathan Morris, a broker at Finacor in Paris.
He said he advised buying ratio call-spreads -- buying an upside call, and then selling two further upside calls.

"If PIBOR rallies, then the long call will hold its value as a downside option, and the two upside calls will see a hike in volatility," he said. "If PIBOR falls, then you can forget the way upside calls, and then concentrate on the one call." -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
